'''Raquel Seruca''' (1962 – 29 May 2022<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Lusa |first=Agência |title=Morreu investigadora da área do cancro Raquel Seruca, aos 59 anos |url=https://observador.pt/2022/05/30/morreu-investigadora-da-area-do-cancro-raquel-seruca-aos-59-anos/ |access-date=2026-07-11 |website=Observador |language=pt-PT}}</ref>) was a Portuguese oncobiologist known for her work on [[stomach cancer]].

== Life ==
Seruca was born and raised in Porto.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ramalho |first=Tiago |title=Morreu Raquel Seruca, "uma inspiração para quem faz investigação" |url=https://www.publico.pt/2022/05/30/ciencia/noticia/morreu-raquel-seruca-vicedirectora-ipatimup-inspiracao-faz-investigacao-2008191 |access-date=31 May 2022 |website=PÚBLICO |date=30 May 2022 |language=pt}}</ref> She graduated in medicine at the [[University of Porto]] before obtaining a PhD in the molecular genetics of stomach cancer in 1995. She was supervised by {{Ill|Manuel Sobrinho Simões|pt}}. She was then a fellow at the [[University of Groningen]] in the human genetics department.<ref name="activa" /><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=i3S {{!}} News |url=https://www.i3s.up.pt/news.php?v=297 |access-date=31 May 2022 |website=www.i3s.up.pt}}</ref>

Seruca and [[Joana Paredes]] led a team that obtained funding three times from the charity [[No Stomach For Cancer]] in 2015, 2017, and 2021<ref name=":0" /> for their research work to create tests to identify mutations in the Caderin-E gene, which is responsible for inherited stomach cancer.<ref name="activa" />

She died in 2022.<ref name=":2" />

== Awards and recognition ==
She was decorated by the Portuguese government with the insignia of Grand Officer of the Order of Infante D. Henrique, in 2009, for her contribution to the study of stomach cancer.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Morreu Raquel Seruca, referência no estudo do cancro gástrico |url=https://www.jn.pt/nacional/morreu-raquel-seruca-referencia-no-estudo-do-cancro-gastrico-14900386.html |access-date=31 May 2022 |website=www.jn.pt |language=pt-PT}}</ref> She was awarded the Benjamin Castelman Award (USCAP) in 2001 and 2012.<ref name=":1" /> She received the Medal of Scientific Merit from the Porto City Council in 2014. In the same year, she was awarded the Femina Award for Merit in Science. In 2021, she won the ACTIVA Women Inspiring Science Award for her contribution to the Comprehensive Cancer Center.<ref name="activa">{{Cite web |date=31 March 2022 |title=Raquel Seruca vence Prémio ACTIVA Mulheres Inspiradoras de Ciência |url=https://noticias.up.pt/raquel-seruca-vence-premio-activa-mulheres-inspiradoras-de-ciencia/ |access-date=31 May 2022 |website=Notícias U.Porto |language=pt-PT}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

The Porto Comprehensive Cancer Center was renamed the Porto Raquel Seruca Comprehensive Cancer Center in her honor.<ref>{{cite web |title=P.CCC Changes Its Name to Honor Researcher Raquel Seruca |url=https://www.i3s.up.pt/news?v=343 |website=i3S |publisher=i3S - Instituto de Investigação e Inovação em Saúde da Universidade do Porto |access-date=5 February 2025}}</ref>
